llm.summary: The skill's code and docs consistently call the Variflight HTTP API and require an API key, but the registry metadata does not declare that credential and the skill will read local OpenClaw/user config files — these mismatches and the implicit credential handling deserve caution before install.

dimensions.detail: The name, README, SKILL.md, and scripts all consistently implement a Variflight API client (flight/train/weather/price/happiness endpoints). That capability matches the description. However, the registry metadata claims no required environment variables or primary credential, whereas both documentation and every script/python wrapper require a VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY — an incoherence between declared requirements and actual needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions and scripts only perform tasks related to the stated purpose: they build request parameters, load an API key from known locations, and POST to the documented ai.variflight.com endpoint. They do read a small set of configuration locations (~/.variflight.json, ~/.config/variflight/config.json, and a legacy OpenClaw env file). Reading these specific config files is within the expected scope for a client that supports multiple config methods, but the code will read the OpenClaw env file if present — worth noting because that file may contain other workspace environment values.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), and included code is zero-dependency Python and shell scripts — no downloads or archive extraction. SKILL.md suggests git cloning from a GitHub repo (https://github.com/variflight-ai/variflight-skill.git) but the package registry 'Source' and 'Homepage' are marked unknown/none. The lack of a verified source URL in the skill metadata is a mild concern: verify the upstream repo and author before cloning/executing scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: All runtime code and docs require an API key (VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY) and support passing it via CLI, env, or config file, but the registry metadata does not list any required env vars or a primary credential. This mismatch means automated policy checks may not prompt for an API key, causing surprise when the skill reads local config files. Additionally, the code prefers a legacy OpenClaw env file (~/.openclaw/workspace/.env.variflight) and will read it if present — that file could contain unrelated secrets in some users' setups, so relying on it may expose more sensitive local config to the skill's loader logic.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and does not declare disableModelInvocation, so it uses default behavior (can be invoked by the model when eligible). This is normal for an integration; however, because the skill will accept an API key from local files and then use it to make outbound network requests, allow-model-invocation combined with unexpected credential-reading (see above) should be considered when enabling autonomous use.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill's code and docs consistently talk to ai.variflight.com and require a VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY, but the registry metadata does not declare that requirement — that's the main mismatch. Before installing:

- Verify the upstream source: confirm the GitHub repo (variflight-ai/variflight-skill) and the publisher identity; do not run scripts from unknown origins.
- Understand that the scripts will read config in these locations (priority order): ./ .variflight.json, ~/.variflight.json, ~/.config/variflight/config.json, and a legacy OpenClaw env file (~/.openclaw/workspace/.env.variflight). If you keep other secrets in that OpenClaw env file, consider moving them or avoid using that file.
- Provide the API key via an explicit environment variable or project config (VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY) rather than leaving it in shared workspace env files.
- Note the skill will POST requests (including your API key in the X-VARIFLIGHT-KEY header) to https://ai.variflight.com; only install if you trust that service and the API key will be accepted there.
- Ask the publisher to update the skill metadata to declare VARIFLIGHT_API_KEY as a required credential / primaryEnv so automated checks and prompts work correctly.

Given the coherent implementation but the metadata mismatch and config-file behavior, treat this as suspicious (not clearly malicious), verify the source, and correct or isolate credential storage before use.
